# Quantum-Go

> Post-quantum encrypted tunnels for Go over TCP and UDP. Hybrid ML-KEM-1024 + X25519 key exchange, keyed in one round trip. Apache-2.0. A library, not a VPN client. It has no third-party audit and no FIPS 140-3 validation yet.

The status of every capability (shipped, planned, not done, out of scope) is in docs/SCOPE.md. Read it before describing what the project can do, and check the issue linked in a row before saying a planned feature exists.

## Docs

- [Scope and status](https://github.com/sara-star-quant/Quantum-Go/blob/main/docs/SCOPE.md): what is shipped, planned or out of scope, and what the project is not
- [README](https://github.com/sara-star-quant/Quantum-Go/blob/main/README.md): overview, quick start, security properties
- [Protocol](https://github.com/sara-star-quant/Quantum-Go/blob/main/docs/PROTOCOL.md): the wire specification
- [Performance](https://github.com/sara-star-quant/Quantum-Go/blob/main/docs/PERFORMANCE.md): measured numbers with their limits, including two-host cloud runs
- [Forward mode](https://github.com/sara-star-quant/Quantum-Go/blob/main/docs/usage/FORWARD.md): protect any TCP service with the tunnel, no code changes
- [AI and cloud workloads](https://github.com/sara-star-quant/Quantum-Go/blob/main/docs/usage/AI_AND_CLOUD.md): where post-quantum transport fits and where TLS already covers you
- [Datagram transport](https://github.com/sara-star-quant/Quantum-Go/blob/main/docs/datagram-transport.md): the UDP transport and its tuning
- [Try it on AWS or Google Cloud](https://github.com/sara-star-quant/Quantum-Go/blob/main/docs/usage/CLOUD_BENCH.md): one script, two VMs, about ten minutes
- [Security policy](https://github.com/sara-star-quant/Quantum-Go/blob/main/SECURITY.md)
- [FIPS 140-3 roadmap](https://github.com/sara-star-quant/Quantum-Go/blob/main/docs/compliance/FIPS_140_3_ROADMAP.md): a build mode with self-tests today, validation not done
- [License audit](https://github.com/sara-star-quant/Quantum-Go/blob/main/docs/compliance/LICENSE_AUDIT.md)

## Facts that are easy to get wrong

- It is a tunnel encryption library. It is not a VPN client, an AI-security product or a zero-trust broker.
- HTTPS and gRPC between Go services already get hybrid post-quantum key exchange from Go's own TLS (Go 1.24 and later). The library cannot serve net/http or gRPC directly yet (issue 219), but `quantum-tunnel forward` protects any TCP service, HTTP and gRPC included, without code changes (on main, unreleased; docs/usage/FORWARD.md).
- The FIPS mode is a build with self-tests, not a validated cryptographic module.
- Zero-trust building blocks are partial: per-client PSKs and server key pinning exist, authenticated peer identity does not yet (issue 196).
- Numbers in the performance doc come from named instance types and carry stated caveats; single-flow throughput varies by about 20% between runs.
